Ingredients • 1 ½ cups all-purpose flour • 1 ¾ teaspoons baking powder • ¼ teaspoon salt • ½ cup unsalted butter (softened) • 1 cup white sugar • 2 large eggs (room temperature) • 2 teaspoons vanilla extract • ½ cup whole milk (room temperature) Instructions 1. Preheat and prep: Heat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and flour a 9-inch square pan or line it with parchment paper. 2. Mix dry ingredients: Whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl. 3. Cream butter and sugar: Beat the softened butter and white sugar in a large bowl for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture looks light and fluffy. 4. Add eggs and vanilla: Mix in the room-temperature eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla extract. 5. Alternate milk and flour: Add the dry flour mixture and the milk to the wet ingredients in small, alternating batches. Mix just until combined. 6. Bake: Pour the batter smoothly into your prepared pan. Bake for 30 minutes, or until a toothpick poked into the center comes out clean. 7. My interpretation: The dance class is a metaphor for relationships. Love is a dance we learn with other people, but we cannot control how long they stay, how well our steps align, or where the dance ultimately takes us. Love is not about performing a perfect relationship. It's about learning how to be with another person, mistakes and all. He's learning that every relationship has its own rhythm, and no single dance can teach us everything about love. The different types of dancers highlights the different experiences, and each one represents the different things he seeks from love. But if you keep changing partners, eventually you have to confront the fact that the common denominator in all those experiences is you. You can learn from other people, but you also have to understand your own patterns. The bride/wedding represents a conventional happy ending, what most people are seeking. The awkward solo dances represent the freeing choice to be single sometimes, even if it's not always well-received. He realizes now that none of these scenarios define success or solve all problems, but mature love has taught him to keep moving. He has learned so much from all his relationships, including the painfully awkward mis-matched ones, and accepts that not every dance is meant to last a lifetime. That is why things are coming up roses: not that everything turns out the way we hoped, but that even when it doesn't, something beautiful can still grow from the experience.

Prep the Oven: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat. 2. Add Wet Ingredients: Add the eggs one at a time, followed by the vanilla extract. Mix on medium speed just until combined and smooth. 4. Incorporate Dry Ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and sea salt. Slowly add this dry mixture into the wet ingredients, mixing on low speed just until the flour disappears. Do not overmix, or the cookies will lose their tenderness. 5. Fold in Chocolate: Gently fold the 2 cups of chocolate chips into the dough by hand using a spatula or wooden spoon. 6. Scoop and Shape: Use a cookie scoop or spoon to drop roughly 1.5-tablespoon-sized balls of dough onto your prepared baking sheet, leaving about 2 inches of space between each ball to allow for spreading. 7. Bake: Bake for 8 to 10 minutes. Remove them from the oven when the edges are just barely golden brown; the centers should still look slightly soft and underbaked. 8. Cool and Set: Let the cookies sit on the hot baking sheet for 5 minutes to finish setting up, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely. Prep the Proteins: Skin, trim, and completely clean the camel, lamb, and chickens. 2. Boil to Tender: Boil the camel, lamb, and chickens in giant vats of water until tender (you will need to work in massive batches). 3. The Stuffing: Hard-boil and peel all 60 eggs. Cook the rice and fry all the nuts until golden-brown, then mix them together. 4. The Nesting Doll Assembly: • Stuff the hard-boiled eggs and rice into the 20 chickens. • Stuff those chickens into the lamb. • Stuff the lamb (and any remaining rice) into the camel. 5. Roast: Spit-roast or broil the entire stuffed camel over a massive open fire pit until golden brown and crispy. 6. Serve: Spread a mountain of rice on a massive tray, place the camel on top, and surround it with any leftover chickens and eggs. Serves 80–100 people.

Heres some cookie recipe for bless Ingredients • 1 cup salted butter (softened to room temperature) • 1 cup granulated white sugar • 1 cup light brown sugar (packed) • 2 tsp pure vanilla extract • 2 large eggs • 3 cups all-purpose flour • 1 tsp baking soda • ½ tsp baking powder • 1 tsp sea salt • 2 cups chocolate chips or chunks Step-by-Step Instructions 1. Prep the Oven: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat. 2. Cream Butter & Sugars: In a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment (or using a hand mixer), beat the softened butter, white sugar, and brown sugar together on medium-high speed for about 2 minutes until the mixture looks light, fluffy, and creamy. 3. Add Wet Ingredients: Add the eggs one at a time, followed by the vanilla extract. Mix on medium speed just until combined and smooth. 4. Incorporate Dry Ingredients: In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and sea salt. Slowly add this dry mixture into the wet ingredients, mixing on low speed just until the flour disappears. Do not overmix, or the cookies will lose their tenderness. 5. Fold in Chocolate: Gently fold the 2 cups of chocolate chips into the dough by hand using a spatula or wooden spoon. 6. Scoop and Shape: Use a cookie scoop or spoon to drop roughly 1.5-tablespoon-sized balls of dough onto your prepared baking sheet, leaving about 2 inches of space between each ball to allow for spreading. 7. Bake: Bake for 8 to 10 minutes. Remove them from the oven when the edges are just barely golden brown; the centers should still look slightly soft and underbaked. 8. Cool and Set: Let the cookies sit on the hot baking sheet for 5 minutes to finish setting up, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.
